exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Period of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function

question.explanation:
Given a function of the form $y = A\tan(Bx +C) + D,$ the period is $\dfrac{\pi}{B}.$

In our case, we have that $B=\dfrac{3}{4}.$ Therefore, the period is $\dfrac{\pi}{\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)}=\dfrac {4\pi}{3}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding a General Expression for the Zeros of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function

question.text: Which of the following expressions gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x) = \cot \left(2x + \dfrac \pi 2\right)?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
The zeros of $y=\cot x$ are given by

\[ x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi, \] where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x) = \cot \left(2x + \dfrac \pi 2\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left(2x+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right).$ This gives

\[ 2x +\dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi. \]

Solving for $x,$ we get

\begin{align*} 2x +\dfrac{\pi}{2} &= \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\\[5pt] 2x &= \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\\[5pt] 2x &= n\pi\\[5pt] x & = \dfrac{n\pi}{2} . \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x = \dfrac{n\pi}{2} ,$ where $n$ is an integer.

question.text: Which of the following expressions gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x) = 2\cot \left(\dfrac x 2 + \dfrac \pi 4\right)?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
The zeros of $y=\cot x$ are given by

\[ x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi, \] where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x) = 2\cot \left(\dfrac x 2 + \dfrac \pi 4\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left(\dfrac x 2+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right).$ This gives

\[ \dfrac x 2+\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi. \]

Solving for $x,$ we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac x 2+\dfrac{\pi}{4} &= \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\\[5pt] \dfrac x 2 &= \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\\[5pt] \dfrac x 2 &= \dfrac{\pi}{4} + n\pi\\[5pt] x & = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + 2n\pi. \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + 2n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.

exampleAnswers.title: Finding a General Expression for the Asymptotes of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function

question.text: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x) = 3\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{6}\right)?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
The asymptotes of $y=\tan x$ are given by the expression

\[ x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi, \] where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $3\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{6}\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left(\dfrac{x}{6}\right).$ This gives \[ \dfrac{x}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi. \]

Solving for $x,$ we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{x}{6} & = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi \\[5pt] x & = 3\pi + 6n\pi. \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x = 3\pi + 6n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.

question.text: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x)=\dfrac{2}{3}\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right),$ where $x$ is measured in degrees?. Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
The asymptotes of $y=\tan x$ are given by the expression

\[ x =90^\circ + n\cdot 180^\circ, \] where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $\dfrac{2}{3}\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left( \dfrac{x}{4}\right).$ This gives

\[ \dfrac{x}{4} =90^\circ + n\cdot 180^\circ. \]

Solving for $x,$ we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{x}{4} &=90^\circ + n\cdot 180^\circ \\[5pt] x &=360^\circ + n\cdot 720^\circ. \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x =360^\circ + n\cdot 720^\circ,$ where $n$ is an integer.

question.text: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x)=\tan(3x)+2?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
The asymptotes of $y=\tan x$ are given by the expression

\[ x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi, \] where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $\tan(3x)+2,$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left( 3x \right).$ This gives

\[ 3x =\dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi. \]

Solving for $x,$ we get

\begin{align*} 3x &=\dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi \\[5pt] x &=\dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{n\pi}{3}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x =\dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{n\pi}{3},$ where $n$ is an integer.

exampleAnswers.title: Finding a General Expression for the Domain of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function

question.text: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=\cot\left(\dfrac{x}{4}-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
The domain of $y=\cot x$ is given by \[ x \neq n\pi, \] where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $\cot\left(\dfrac{x}{4}-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left(\dfrac{x}{4}-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right).$ This gives \[ \dfrac{x}{4}-\dfrac{\pi}{2} \neq n\pi. \]

Solving for $x,$ we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{x}{4}-\dfrac{\pi}{2} &\neq n\pi \\[5pt] \dfrac{x}{4} &\neq \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi \\[5pt] x & = 2\pi + 4n\pi. \end{align*}

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x \neq 2\pi + 4n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.

example.title: Finding a General Expression for the Domain of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function

question.text: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=3\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)-1?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
The domain of $y=\tan x$ is given by

\[ x \neq \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi , \] where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $3\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)-1,$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left( x-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right).$ This gives \[ x-\dfrac{\pi}{3} \neq \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi . \]

Solving for $x,$ we get

\begin{align*} x-\dfrac{\pi}{3} &\neq \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi \\[5pt] x &\neq \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\\[5pt] x &\neq \dfrac{5\pi}{6} + n\pi . \end{align*}

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x \neq \dfrac{5\pi}{6} + n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.

example.title: Finding a General Expression for the Domain of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function

question.text: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=\tan\left(\dfrac x 3\right)+1?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
The domain of $y=\tan x$ is given by

\[ x \neq \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi, \] where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $\tan\left(\dfrac x 3\right)+1,$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left( \dfrac x 3 \right).$ This gives \[ \dfrac x 3 \neq \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi. \]

Solving for $x,$ we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac x 3 &\neq \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi \\[5pt] % x &\neq \dfrac{3\cdot\pi}{2} + 3n\pi \\[5pt] x &\neq \dfrac{3\pi}{2} + 3n\pi. \end{align*}

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x \neq \dfrac{3\pi}{2} + 3n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.
